tabs.title: Platform Apps setup
tabs.summary: Enter Credovation’s Meta, LinkedIn and Google apps once — every company then connects with a sign-in button.
tabs.html:
How it works

The Super Admin sets up one sign-in app per platform, once, in Settings → Platform Apps. After that, every company connects its own accounts by clicking Connect in Integration. It signs in on the platform’s own page and never sees App IDs or secrets.

Until a platform is saved, companies see that channel as “Not enabled yet”, with no Connect button.

Already using these apps for SMC? You can use the same Meta, LinkedIn and Google apps. Enter the same IDs and secrets here. In each app, also add this platform’s callback URL (below), and the lead permissions listed for that platform.

On each card:

  1. Paste the ID and Secret → Save.
  2. Register the callback URL(s) shown on the card in the platform’s developer console, exactly as shown (https, no trailing slash).
  3. Click Test and fix anything marked in red.
Platform Callback URL Webhook URL
Meta (Facebook & Instagram) {{metaCallback}} {{metaWebhook}}
LinkedIn {{linkedinCallback}} {{linkedinWebhook}}
Google {{googleCallback}} —

Meta — Facebook Lead Ads and Instagram Lead Ads

  1. developers.facebook.com → My Apps → open the Credovation app, or Create app (type Business).
  2. Add the use cases for Lead Ads (capture and manage ad leads) and Facebook Login for Business. Menu names can change slightly when Meta updates its dashboard.
  3. Facebook Login for Business → Settings → Valid OAuth Redirect URIs → add {{metaCallback}}.
  4. App settings → Basic:
    • App Domains: add {{baseDomain}}
    • Privacy Policy URL: {{privacyUrl}}
    • Terms of Service URL: {{termsUrl}}
    • User data deletion → Data deletion instructions URL: {{dataDeletionUrl}}
    • Copy the App ID and App Secret into the Meta card → Save.
  5. Click Test. It checks the ID and secret, checks App Domains, and subscribes the lead webhook for you (Page → leadgen → {{metaWebhook}}). If it can’t, do it by hand: Webhooks → Page → Subscribe, with the Callback URL {{metaWebhook}} and the Verify token from the card, then subscribe to leadgen.
  6. Switch the app to Live.
  7. Permissions the connectors ask for: leads_retrieval, pages_show_list, pages_read_engagement, pages_manage_metadata, pages_manage_ads, ads_management and business_management. Instagram also asks for instagram_basic.
  8. For companies other than Credovation:
    • Until Meta approves Advanced Access for the permissions above, only people with a role on the app (Administrators, Developers, Testers) can connect.
    • To get Advanced Access: App Review → Permissions and Features → request Advanced Access for each permission (screen recording plus use-case text), and complete Business Verification of Credovation.
    • Until it’s approved, add client users as Testers (App roles → Roles).

Use-case text for App Review: “CredoOne is a lead management system. A business connects its Facebook Page so that the people who fill its Lead Ad forms are added to its CRM as leads. We list the user’s Pages so they can choose which to connect, subscribe the Page to leadgen webhooks and read each lead’s form answers.”

Screen recording (1–3 min):

  1. Sign in to the company console → Integration → Facebook Lead Ads → Connect.
  2. Consent notice → Facebook login → permission screen → pick the Page → Connected.
  3. Create a test lead with the Lead Ads Testing Tool → the lead appears in Leads.

LinkedIn — Lead Gen Forms

  1. linkedin.com/developers/apps → open the Credovation app, or Create app linked to the Credovation Company Page. A Page admin must Verify it (Settings tab).
  2. Auth tab:
    • Authorized redirect URLs → add {{linkedinCallback}}.
    • Copy the Client ID and Client Secret into the LinkedIn card → Save → Test.
  3. Products tab → request Lead Sync API. LinkedIn reviews this. If it can’t be added next to the app’s other products, create a second app just for it and use that one here.
  4. The scopes used are r_marketing_leadgen_automation, r_ads and r_organization_admin.
  5. Webhooks tab (when available for the app) → add {{linkedinWebhook}}. LinkedIn validates it automatically, and responses then arrive within seconds. Without it, responses are fetched every 15 minutes.

LinkedIn logins last about 60 days. After that, companies see “Reconnect”.

Google — Google Sheets / Google Forms

  1. console.cloud.google.com → the Credovation project.
  2. APIs & Services → Library → enable Google Sheets API.
  3. OAuth consent screen (Google Auth Platform):
    • Data access → add the scope https://www.googleapis.com/auth/spreadsheets.readonly.
    • Home page {{platformUrl}}, privacy {{privacyUrl}}, terms {{termsUrl}}, and the authorised domain for {{baseDomain}}.
    • Audience → Publish app.
  4. Credentials → OAuth client ID (Web application) → Authorised redirect URIs → add {{googleCallback}}. Copy the Client ID and Client Secret into the Google card → Save → Test.
  5. Until Google verifies the app, users see “Google hasn’t verified this app” and click Advanced → Go to CredoOne. This works for up to 100 users. Submit for verification to remove the warning.

Privacy contact

The Privacy contact card sets the email, grievance officer, legal name and address. They appear on every consent notice and on the public pages the platform apps link to:

  • {{privacyUrl}}
  • {{termsUrl}}
  • {{dataDeletionUrl}}

It starts as support@credovation.tech. Change it if privacy requests should go elsewhere. Currently: {{privacyEmail}}.

## How it works

The Super Admin sets up **one sign-in app per platform**, once, in **Settings → Platform Apps**. After that, every company connects its own accounts by clicking **Connect** in **Integration**. It signs in on the platform’s own page and never sees App IDs or secrets.

Until a platform is saved, companies see that channel as **“Not enabled yet”**, with no Connect button.

> **Already using these apps for SMC?** You can use the **same** Meta, LinkedIn and Google apps. Enter the same IDs and secrets here. In each app, also add this platform’s callback URL (below), and the lead permissions listed for that platform.

On each card:
1. Paste the **ID** and **Secret** → **Save**.
2. Register the **callback URL(s)** shown on the card in the platform’s developer console, exactly as shown (https, no trailing slash).
3. Click **Test** and fix anything marked in red.

| Platform | Callback URL | Webhook URL |
|---|---|---|
| Meta (Facebook & Instagram) | `{{metaCallback}}` | `{{metaWebhook}}` |
| LinkedIn | `{{linkedinCallback}}` | `{{linkedinWebhook}}` |
| Google | `{{googleCallback}}` | — |

## Meta — Facebook Lead Ads and Instagram Lead Ads

1. developers.facebook.com → **My Apps** → open the Credovation app, or **Create app** (type **Business**).
2. Add the use cases for **Lead Ads** (capture and manage ad leads) and **Facebook Login for Business**. Menu names can change slightly when Meta updates its dashboard.
3. **Facebook Login for Business → Settings → Valid OAuth Redirect URIs** → add `{{metaCallback}}`.
4. **App settings → Basic**:
   - App Domains: add `{{baseDomain}}`
   - Privacy Policy URL: `{{privacyUrl}}`
   - Terms of Service URL: `{{termsUrl}}`
   - User data deletion → Data deletion instructions URL: `{{dataDeletionUrl}}`
   - Copy the **App ID** and **App Secret** into the Meta card → **Save**.
5. Click **Test**. It checks the ID and secret, checks App Domains, and **subscribes the lead webhook for you** (Page → `leadgen` → `{{metaWebhook}}`). If it can’t, do it by hand: **Webhooks → Page → Subscribe**, with the Callback URL `{{metaWebhook}}` and the **Verify token** from the card, then subscribe to **leadgen**.
6. Switch the app to **Live**.
7. **Permissions the connectors ask for:** `leads_retrieval`, `pages_show_list`, `pages_read_engagement`, `pages_manage_metadata`, `pages_manage_ads`, `ads_management` and `business_management`. Instagram also asks for `instagram_basic`.
8. **For companies other than Credovation:**
   - Until Meta approves **Advanced Access** for the permissions above, only people with a role on the app (Administrators, Developers, Testers) can connect.
   - To get Advanced Access: **App Review → Permissions and Features** → request Advanced Access for each permission (screen recording plus use-case text), and complete **Business Verification** of Credovation.
   - Until it’s approved, add client users as **Testers** (App roles → Roles).

**Use-case text for App Review:** “CredoOne is a lead management system. A business connects its Facebook Page so that the people who fill its Lead Ad forms are added to its CRM as leads. We list the user’s Pages so they can choose which to connect, subscribe the Page to leadgen webhooks and read each lead’s form answers.”

**Screen recording (1–3 min):**
1. Sign in to the company console → Integration → Facebook Lead Ads → Connect.
2. Consent notice → Facebook login → permission screen → pick the Page → Connected.
3. Create a test lead with the Lead Ads Testing Tool → the lead appears in Leads.

## LinkedIn — Lead Gen Forms

1. linkedin.com/developers/apps → open the Credovation app, or **Create app** linked to the Credovation Company Page. A Page admin must **Verify** it (Settings tab).
2. **Auth** tab:
   - Authorized redirect URLs → add `{{linkedinCallback}}`.
   - Copy the **Client ID** and **Client Secret** into the LinkedIn card → **Save** → **Test**.
3. **Products** tab → request **Lead Sync API**. LinkedIn reviews this. If it can’t be added next to the app’s other products, create a second app just for it and use that one here.
4. The scopes used are `r_marketing_leadgen_automation`, `r_ads` and `r_organization_admin`.
5. **Webhooks** tab (when available for the app) → add `{{linkedinWebhook}}`. LinkedIn validates it automatically, and responses then arrive within seconds. Without it, responses are fetched every 15 minutes.

LinkedIn logins last about 60 days. After that, companies see **“Reconnect”**.

## Google — Google Sheets / Google Forms

1. console.cloud.google.com → the Credovation project.
2. **APIs & Services → Library** → enable **Google Sheets API**.
3. **OAuth consent screen** (Google Auth Platform):
   - Data access → add the scope `https://www.googleapis.com/auth/spreadsheets.readonly`.
   - Home page `{{platformUrl}}`, privacy `{{privacyUrl}}`, terms `{{termsUrl}}`, and the authorised domain for `{{baseDomain}}`.
   - Audience → **Publish app**.
4. **Credentials → OAuth client ID (Web application)** → Authorised redirect URIs → add `{{googleCallback}}`. Copy the **Client ID** and **Client Secret** into the Google card → **Save** → **Test**.
5. Until Google verifies the app, users see “Google hasn’t verified this app” and click **Advanced → Go to CredoOne**. This works for up to 100 users. Submit for verification to remove the warning.

## Privacy contact

The **Privacy contact** card sets the email, grievance officer, legal name and address. They appear on every consent notice and on the public pages the platform apps link to:
- `{{privacyUrl}}`
- `{{termsUrl}}`
- `{{dataDeletionUrl}}`

It starts as `support@credovation.tech`. Change it if privacy requests should go elsewhere. Currently: **{{privacyEmail}}**.

tabs.title: Connecting channels
tabs.summary: What a company does to connect Facebook, Instagram, LinkedIn or Google Sheets — and what to tell them.
tabs.html:
For company users (2 minutes)

  1. Integration → the channel card → Connect with Facebook / LinkedIn / Google.
  2. Read the consent notice (DPDP Act). Click I agree to all & connect, or tick each purpose and click Continue. Nothing is pre-ticked: consent must be a clear action. Who agreed, when, from which IP and which notice version are all recorded.
  3. A secure window opens on facebook.com / linkedin.com / accounts.google.com. Sign in with your own ID and password. CredoOne never sees them.
  4. On the platform’s screen, keep every permission box ticked, and select your Pages (Facebook) or Business.
  5. Back in CredoOne, pick what to connect:
    • Facebook: Pages
    • Instagram: Instagram professional accounts
    • LinkedIn: ad accounts and Pages
    • Google: paste the sheet link and pick the tab
  6. Click Connect. Recent leads are fetched straight away, then:
    • Facebook / Instagram: new leads arrive in seconds (Page lead webhook), with a check every 15 minutes as a safety net.
    • LinkedIn: instant when LinkedIn notifications are on, otherwise every 15 minutes.
    • Google Sheets: new rows every 15 minutes. Each row is read once.

Facebook and Instagram are separate connectors

They sign in the same way (Instagram lead ads are delivered through Facebook), but each has its own card, its own Pages and accounts, and its own stats.

When both are connected for the same Page:

  • Facebook-placement leads go to Facebook Lead Ads.
  • Instagram-placement leads go to Instagram Lead Ads.

When only one of them is connected, it receives both placements, so no lead is lost.

Disconnect = withdraw consent

Disconnect on the connector:

  • unsubscribes the Pages
  • deletes the stored login immediately
  • stops new leads

Leads already received stay. Reconnect at any time.

Status you may see

Status Meaning What to do
Not enabled yet The Super Admin hasn’t saved that platform in Platform Apps Super Admin → Platform Apps
Connected Leads are flowing —
Reconnect needed / Login expired The platform login expired or was revoked (LinkedIn: about 60 days) Open the connector → Reconnect
Disconnected Consent was withdrawn Reconnect, or delete the connector
“Real-time off … fetched every 15 minutes” on a Page The Page couldn’t be subscribed to the lead webhook Check you have the Advertise task on the Page; allow CredoOne in Meta Business Suite → Settings → Integrations → Leads access

## For company users (2 minutes)

1. **Integration** → the channel card → **Connect with Facebook / LinkedIn / Google**.
2. Read the **consent notice (DPDP Act)**. Click **I agree to all & connect**, or tick each purpose and click **Continue**. Nothing is pre-ticked: consent must be a clear action. Who agreed, when, from which IP and which notice version are all recorded.
3. A secure window opens on **facebook.com / linkedin.com / accounts.google.com**. Sign in with your **own** ID and password. CredoOne never sees them.
4. On the platform’s screen, **keep every permission box ticked**, and select your Pages (Facebook) or Business.
5. Back in CredoOne, pick what to connect:
   - **Facebook:** Pages
   - **Instagram:** Instagram professional accounts
   - **LinkedIn:** ad accounts and Pages
   - **Google:** paste the sheet link and pick the tab
6. Click **Connect**. Recent leads are fetched straight away, then:
   - **Facebook / Instagram:** new leads arrive in seconds (Page lead webhook), with a check every 15 minutes as a safety net.
   - **LinkedIn:** instant when LinkedIn notifications are on, otherwise every 15 minutes.
   - **Google Sheets:** new rows every 15 minutes. Each row is read once.

## Facebook and Instagram are separate connectors

They sign in the same way (Instagram lead ads are delivered through Facebook), but each has its own card, its own Pages and accounts, and its own stats.

When both are connected for the same Page:
- Facebook-placement leads go to **Facebook Lead Ads**.
- Instagram-placement leads go to **Instagram Lead Ads**.

When only one of them is connected, it receives both placements, so no lead is lost.

## Disconnect = withdraw consent

**Disconnect** on the connector:
- unsubscribes the Pages
- deletes the stored login immediately
- stops new leads

Leads already received stay. **Reconnect** at any time.

## Status you may see

| Status | Meaning | What to do |
|---|---|---|
| Not enabled yet | The Super Admin hasn’t saved that platform in Platform Apps | Super Admin → Platform Apps |
| Connected | Leads are flowing | — |
| Reconnect needed / Login expired | The platform login expired or was revoked (LinkedIn: about 60 days) | Open the connector → **Reconnect** |
| Disconnected | Consent was withdrawn | **Reconnect**, or delete the connector |
| “Real-time off … fetched every 15 minutes” on a Page | The Page couldn’t be subscribed to the lead webhook | Check you have the Advertise task on the Page; allow CredoOne in Meta Business Suite → Settings → Integrations → **Leads access** |

tabs.title: REST API & webhooks
tabs.summary: Website / landing-page forms, WhatsApp Business Platform and generic REST — all authenticated with the connector’s API key.
tabs.html:
One model for every push channel

Website / Landing Page Form, WhatsApp Business Platform and REST API / Webhook all work the same way: the sender POSTs to the connector’s endpoint and proves it is allowed with the connector’s API key.

Any one of these authenticates the request:

  • header x-api-key: <API key>
  • ?key=<API key> in the URL, for senders that can’t set headers (Meta Cloud API, plain HTML forms)
  • x-signature: sha256=<HMAC-SHA256 of the raw body, keyed with the API key>

Calls without a valid key get 401. Fields like name, phone, mobile, email, message, city and utm_* are mapped automatically. Use Field mapping for anything else.

curl -X POST '{{platformUrl}}/api/intake/<connector key>' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'x-api-key: <API key>' \
  -H 'Idempotency-Key: form-1042' \
  -d '{"name":"Riya Sen","phone":"9876543210","email":"riya@example.com","message":"Full body checkup","consent":"yes"}'

Responses:

  • 200 — created or merged (includes leadId)
  • 202 — accepted but failed; it is retried automatically every 15 minutes
  • 401 — wrong or missing key
  • 429 — slow down

Send the same Idempotency-Key header on retries, and the lead is never duplicated.

Website / Landing Page Form

  • From your server or form plugin (Elementor, Contact Form 7, Webflow, Wix): add a webhook to the endpoint with the x-api-key header, or put ?key= in the URL.
  • Plain HTML form: action="<endpoint>?key=<API key>". After submitting, people land on the hosted thank-you page.
  • Browser fetch: works too, but the key is visible in the page source. Rotate it if it is misused.

Keep a hidden _hp field: submissions where it is filled in are treated as bots.

WhatsApp Business Platform

  • Meta Cloud API: set the Callback URL to <endpoint>?key=<API key> and the Verify token to the API key, then subscribe to messages.
  • BSPs (Interakt, AiSensy, Gupshup, WATI…): point the incoming-message webhook at the endpoint and add the x-api-key header.

Older connectors

Website-form and WhatsApp connectors created before this change still accept deliveries without the key, so live sites don’t break. Their Setup tab shows Require API key: update the form or Callback URL first, then click it.
tabs.md:
## One model for every push channel

**Website / Landing Page Form**, **WhatsApp Business Platform** and **REST API / Webhook** all work the same way: the sender POSTs to the connector’s **endpoint** and proves it is allowed with the connector’s **API key**.

Any one of these authenticates the request:
- header `x-api-key: <API key>`
- `?key=<API key>` in the URL, for senders that can’t set headers (Meta Cloud API, plain HTML forms)
- `x-signature: sha256=<HMAC-SHA256 of the raw body, keyed with the API key>`

Calls without a valid key get **401**. Fields like name, phone, mobile, email, message, city and utm_* are mapped automatically. Use **Field mapping** for anything else.

```
curl -X POST '{{platformUrl}}/api/intake/<connector key>' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'x-api-key: <API key>' \
  -H 'Idempotency-Key: form-1042' \
  -d '{"name":"Riya Sen","phone":"9876543210","email":"riya@example.com","message":"Full body checkup","consent":"yes"}'
```

Responses:
- **200** — created or merged (includes `leadId`)
- **202** — accepted but failed; it is retried automatically every 15 minutes
- **401** — wrong or missing key
- **429** — slow down

Send the same `Idempotency-Key` header on retries, and the lead is never duplicated.

## Website / Landing Page Form

- **From your server or form plugin** (Elementor, Contact Form 7, Webflow, Wix): add a webhook to the endpoint with the `x-api-key` header, or put `?key=` in the URL.
- **Plain HTML form:** `action="<endpoint>?key=<API key>"`. After submitting, people land on the hosted thank-you page.
- **Browser fetch:** works too, but the key is visible in the page source. Rotate it if it is misused.

Keep a hidden `_hp` field: submissions where it is filled in are treated as bots.

## WhatsApp Business Platform

- **Meta Cloud API:** set the Callback URL to `<endpoint>?key=<API key>` and the Verify token to the API key, then subscribe to **messages**.
- **BSPs** (Interakt, AiSensy, Gupshup, WATI…): point the incoming-message webhook at the endpoint and add the `x-api-key` header.

## Older connectors

Website-form and WhatsApp connectors created before this change still accept deliveries without the key, so live sites don’t break. Their Setup tab shows **Require API key**: update the form or Callback URL first, then click it.

tabs.title: Company modules & access
tabs.summary: Pause or restrict any module or sub-module for one company, on top of its plan.
tabs.html:
Where

Company → Edit (or Create) → Modules tab.

Every module and sub-module comes from the module registry, so new ones appear here automatically after each deploy.

Three settings per row

Setting Effect
Plan default (modules) / Follows module (sub-modules) Uses the plan’s access. Change the plan and this follows.
Custom Tick exactly which of Create, Read, Update and Delete this company gets. You can restrict below the plan, or give more than the plan. A sub-module can never go beyond its module.
Paused Switches the module (or sub-module) off for this company. The module stays in its menu marked Paused and shows a notice; its data is kept. Set it back to Plan default to resume.

What it affects

  • Every user of the company, the owner included. Changes apply within about 30 seconds, with no sign-out needed.
  • Role Management inside the company: the grid is capped by these settings, so paused or restricted actions can’t be granted. Roles saved earlier are capped automatically.
  • The API: paused or restricted actions are refused on the server, not only hidden in the screens.

Reset all to plan removes every override for the company.

tabs.title: Troubleshooting
tabs.summary: The exact messages platforms show, why, and the fix.
tabs.html:
First check, always: Super Admin → Platform Apps → Test on the platform. It confirms the ID and secret, checks App Domains and the lead webhook (Meta), and lists the exact URLs to register.

What you see Cause Fix
Card says “Not enabled yet” That platform isn’t saved in Platform Apps Platform Apps → enter the ID and secret → Save → Test
Popup: “This sign-in link has expired” More than an hour passed, or the link was reused Click Connect again
Nothing opens after “I agree” The browser blocked the popup Use Open the sign-in window, or allow popups for the site
Facebook: “URL blocked” / redirect URI is not whitelisted Callback missing in the Meta app Add {{metaCallback}} under Facebook Login for Business → Settings → Valid OAuth Redirect URIs
Facebook: “Feature unavailable … updating additional details for this app” The person has no role on the Meta app, and Advanced Access isn’t approved yet Add them as a Tester, or get Advanced Access + Business Verification
Facebook: “App not active” App in Development mode Switch the app to Live
Facebook: “Invalid Scopes: leads_retrieval …” The Lead Ads use case isn’t added to the app Add the use case and permissions (Platform Apps setup)
“Connected without a permission we need” A box was unticked on Facebook’s screen Connect again and keep every box ticked
“No Facebook Pages came back” Pages weren’t selected, or the person isn’t a Page admin Reconnect and select the Pages, or ask a Page admin
Instagram account greyed out Not a professional account, or not linked to a Page Switch to Professional and link it to the Facebook Page
Page shows “Real-time off” The Page couldn’t install the app (task or Leads access) Advertise task on the Page; Meta Business Suite → Integrations → Leads access → allow CredoOne. Leads still arrive every 15 minutes.
Leads arrive only every 15 minutes (Meta) The app’s Page leadgen webhook isn’t set Platform Apps → Meta → Test (it sets it), or add it in Webhooks
LinkedIn: “redirect_uri does not match” Callback missing on the Auth tab Add {{linkedinCallback}}
LinkedIn: “unauthorized_scope_error” Lead Sync API not approved for the app Request Lead Sync API in Products
LinkedIn: “No ad accounts or Pages came back” The person lacks an ad-account role Account Manager, Campaign Manager or Leads Manager on the ad account
Google: “Error 400: redirect_uri_mismatch” Callback not on the OAuth client Add {{googleCallback}} under Authorised redirect URIs
Google: “access_denied — app is being tested” Consent screen in Testing Publish the app, or add the user as a test user
Google: “This Google account can’t open that sheet” Sheet not shared with that account Share the sheet, or sign in with its owner
Connector says “Login expired — reconnect” The token expired or was revoked Open the connector → Reconnect
Website form / WhatsApp returns 401 The API key is missing from the call Send x-api-key, or add ?key= to the URL (REST API & webhooks)

tabs.title: What’s new
tabs.html:

## October 2026 — sign-in connectors, Platform Apps, company modules

- **Facebook Lead Ads, Instagram Lead Ads, LinkedIn Lead Gen Forms and Google Sheets / Forms** are now sign-in connectors:
  - Companies click Connect, give consent (DPDP Act), sign in on the platform and pick their Pages, accounts or sheet.
  - No App IDs, secrets or webhook setup for companies.
  - The old Facebook & Instagram App-ID setup is retired; existing connectors keep working.
- **Super Admin → Settings → Platform Apps**:
  - Credovation’s Meta, LinkedIn and Google apps, with a **Test** button that also sets the Meta lead webhook.
  - An editable **Privacy contact** that appears on consent notices and on the new `/privacy`, `/terms` and `/data-deletion` pages.
- **Website / Landing Page Form** and **WhatsApp Business Platform** are now REST API / webhook connectors, authenticated with the API key (older connectors keep working until switched).
- **Company → Modules** tab: pause or restrict any module or sub-module per company, on top of the plan.
- **Knowledge Base** tabs are written as Markdown files in the code (`content/kb`), so they update with every deploy.
  - Each article has **Download .md** and **Copy Markdown**, and **Full guide (.md)** gives every article in one file.
  - The Markdown is rebuilt on every deploy, with that deployment’s addresses filled in.

## October 2026 — earlier

- Role Management sub-modules.
- Client billing renamed to Sales Order, Invoice and Pay-In.
- A pop-up with S3 attachments when an invoice is marked Paid.
- An “S3 storage required” switch per company.
